blocks.text: Analytical chemistry is the science of chemical characterisation. A complete characterisation of a compound includes both qualitative and quantitative analysis: in qualitative analysis the chemist detects or identifies the elements present in a compound, whereas in quantitative analysis the relative amounts of the elements are determined.

blocks.title: The four steps of a quantitative determination
blocks.text: A complete quantitative determination generally has four major steps: obtaining a sample for analysis; separating the desired constituent; measurement and calculation of the results; and drawing conclusions from the analysis.
This chapter discusses some basic separation techniques to be practised in the laboratory.
